I've been growing cotton on this land for most of my life. My father grew it, I grew it, and I know this soil and this climate. Five mu isn't much, but it's mine and it's what my household depends on. Cotton prices have been rough the last few years, but I don't know wheat the way I know cotton — I'm not switching now at 53.

For seed, I'll buy the improved Bt cotton variety from the county seed station, same as I've done the past several years. It handles bollworm better and saves me some spray trips. Not going with the cheapest seed — that's a mistake I made once in my thirties and won't repeat.

I'll deep plough after last season's stalks are chopped under. That's how I've always done it — breaks up the hardpan, buries the pest residue. Rotary is faster but I don't trust it for cotton roots.

For fertilizer, I apply base fertilizer before planting — phosphorus and potassium go in at ploughing, nitrogen I split: some at planting, more at squaring, and a top-dress at boll setting. Roughly 13 kg nitrogen, 6 phosphorus, 6 potassium per mu. My neighbor uses more nitrogen but his cotton lodges in wind. I've learned restraint.

With the well I'll irrigate four times: at seedling establishment if it's dry, at squaring, heavy at flowering and boll set, and one more if August is hot. Five irrigations if it's a drought year.

Pesticide — I scout myself, walk the field every few days. Even with Bt seed, aphids and spider mites still need attention. I'll plan for five applications but I won't spray if I don't see the pressure. Last year I managed with four.

Expected yield around 260 kg seed cotton per mu — that's what I've averaged on this land with good water.
